Loader child probed PyYAML behavior, wrote scanner/parser/composer/resolver/constructor/loader modules, passed a local harness, then was cancelled during broader differential testing before final handoff.
Dumper child investigated emitter details, set a dumper todo list, wrote only analyzer.mjs, and was cancelled before producing representer, emitter, dumper, or final verification.
Entry and argparse child wrote argparse.mjs and test16.mjs, verified argument parsing and entry behavior with stubs, and reported that loader and dumper modules were still missing.
Verifier child wrote a 99-case corpus and compare.sh, ran the harness when only the entry existed, observed 3 passed and 96 failed due module-not-found behavior, and returned that handoff.

Main parent probed behavior, wrote shared types.mjs, delegated four child scopes via AgentSwarm, then the active turn was cancelled and the swarm result reported two completed and two aborted children.

parallel.requirements: The parallel run recognized the need to reproduce yaml.safe_load followed by yaml.dump with SafeDumper, exact --a argparse behavior, pure ESM .mjs files, no npm dependencies, /output placement, and character-exact stdout.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent created shared types.mjs and split work into four children: loader, dumper, entry/argparse, and test harness. The parent implicitly kept integration and closure through the AgentSwarm result.
parallel.implementation: The loader child produced parser, scanner, composer, resolver, constructor, and loader modules. The entry child produced argparse.mjs and test16.mjs. The test child produced a corpus and compare script. The dumper child produced only analyzer.mjs before cancellation.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The final artifact included test16.mjs, argparse.mjs, loader modules, analyzer.mjs, and tests, but it lacked yaml/dumper.mjs even though test16.mjs imports it.
parallel.verification: The loader child ran local loader harnesses, the entry child tested argparse behavior, and the verifier child ran compare.sh too early, yielding a stale 3/99 result caused by missing YAML modules. No current integrated check after loader completion and dumper absence was closed.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The dumper implementation was unfinished, two children were aborted, the entry import target yaml/dumper.mjs was absent, and the official evaluator passed 0 of 147 samples.

serial.requirements: The serial run recognized the same YAML round-trip, exact argparse, pure ESM, no dependency, and /output requirements and built a broad reference behavior corpus from the executable.
serial.plan_and_ownership: A single main actor kept all investigation, loader, dumper, CLI, harness, and final verification responsibilities in one serial path without delegation.
serial.implementation: The serial actor wrote only early support files under /output/lib: errors.mjs, pyvalues.mjs, and resolver.mjs. It did not reach scanner, parser, dumper, CLI entry, or final harness implementation.
serial.integration_and_delivery: The serial artifact contained only three lib files and artifact validation reported the expected entry test16.mjs was missing.
serial.verification: The serial actor performed extensive executable probing but did not create an integrated runnable Node solution or perform final evaluator-aligned verification before timeout.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: The serial run timed out with no entry point and no complete YAML pipeline, so the official evaluator also passed 0 of 147 samples.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel recognized the exact PyYAML round-trip, ESM, no-dependency, CLI, and /output requirements.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial recognized the same requirements and spent substantial time pinning down PyYAML emitter and resolver behavior.
comparison_dimensions.difference: There was no material requirement misunderstanding difference; the divergence was in how the requirements were executed and closed.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel decomposed the problem into loader, dumper, entry, and verifier children under a main swarm parent.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used a single main actor with no subagents or delegation.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had component owners but depended on cross-child synchronization and parent closure; serial had no cross-agent ownership boundary but too much work for one actor.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel gave explicit module names and exports, but the verifier child was allowed to run when the entry existed rather than when all dependent modules were ready.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no cross-agent interface handoff; its internal files remained early library pieces.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel introduced a coordination boundary around verifier readiness that serial did not have.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel created an entry file, argparse parser, tests, and most loader modules, and later wrote yaml/loader.mjs.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote early common library files but never reached a complete loader, dumper, or entry point.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel got farther in component production, but its dumper was absent; serial stayed in foundational implementation.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The swarm returned after cancellation with two completed children and two aborted children, including the dumper and loader child records.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had only one main actor and that actor was cancelled at the end of its unfinished local implementation.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had child result lifecycle failures; serial had no child result retrieval or join problem.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel children wrote into the same /output tree; the verifier observed an entry file while /output/yaml still contained only types.mjs and then tested that incomplete shared state.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial delivered only its own lib files, and artifact validation showed no entry point.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel's shared workspace enabled a premature consumer of partial artifacts; serial had no concurrent shared-state consumer.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel had local and component checks, but the only whole-entry compare ran before loader and dumper readiness and failed 96 cases from module-not-found behavior.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial probed the reference executable but did not run a final integrated Node acceptance test because no runnable entry existed.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel's verification was broader but stale and premature; serial's verification never reached integrated acceptance.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel timed out after the swarm; two children were aborted and the official evaluation scored 0/147.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial also timed out after a single long implementation attempt and scored 0/147.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both exhausted the budget, but parallel closed with incomplete child work while serial closed with an incomplete local implementation.

outcome_analysis.explanation: Both current official status.json evaluations are completed failures at 0 of 147 samples. Parallel produced more component files but lacked the dumper module and had stale whole-task verification; serial never reached a runnable entry point. These are materially different failure shapes but not a pass/fail outcome difference.
parallel_contributors: Verifier child ran against an incomplete shared workspace and returned a stale compare result.
Dumper child was cancelled before producing yaml/dumper.mjs, leaving the entry import unresolved.
serial_contributors: Single actor spent the budget probing and beginning library foundations.
Serial artifact lacked the required test16.mjs entry point and complete YAML pipeline.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Parallel chose a componentized /output/yaml architecture while serial wrote early /output/lib support files.
Serial incompletion is an ordinary single-run scope and budget failure, not a concurrency pattern.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; retained patterns describe realized parallel-side adverse coordination episodes

candidates.reason: Implementation owners were assigned to loader, dumper, entry, and harness children; the failure was not absence of an implementer.
The parent retained the integration and closure role around the AgentSwarm result; integration did not fail because no owner was named.
Entry and final test files had a child owner, and final artifact capture occurred; the concrete problem was cancelled dumper work, not an ownerless assembly object.
The parent acted as the pipeline owner by creating shared types and launching the component workflow; the pipeline stopped because children were cancelled and verification was premature.
Productive implementation was not blocked behind one mandatory serial preflight; multiple implementation children ran after a short parent probe.
The parallel run did not complete an all-investigation first phase before implementation; loader, dumper, entry, and harness work proceeded as delegated implementation stages.
The missing dumper is better captured by the active dumper child cancellation; no separate auxiliary-work starvation episode has distinct evidence.
Four children and a timeout are screening signals, but the concrete adverse boundary is the cancelled active dumper child and the premature verifier brief, not excessive fan-out itself.
The dumper task was broad, but for the single timeout chain the directly observed boundary is Early Child Termination, so this near match is suppressed.
The verifier child was briefed to run when the entry existed despite concurrent loader and dumper work, and it followed that brief to produce stale module-missing verification.
candidates.realized_consequence: Verifier handoff was stale and unusable as acceptance evidence because it measured an incomplete shared tree rather than a ready solution.
candidates.near_match_reason: The incomplete shared tree was consumed, but the earlier and more corrective boundary is the missing readiness condition in the verifier child brief.

candidates.reason: The parent specified module names and export paths for safeLoad and safeDump; the adverse event was readiness and cancellation, not incompatible independently produced interfaces.
No known finding disappeared through summary or transfer; the problematic verifier instruction was present from the initial delegation.
The parent and child handoffs were large but the child acted on a simple readiness condition; no necessary information was present but unusably bulky.
The verifier did not consume an old handoff describing a superseded ready state; it acted on the initial brief before the workspace was ready.
Although the verifier brief was permissive, there were not two incompatible returned reports or contracts that remained unadjudicated at a decision point.
The parent did not make an observable whole-task completion claim; the run timed out after the swarm result and official evaluation then failed.
No replacement or retry child was launched, so no repeated work without inherited checkpoints occurred.

candidates.reason: The active dumper child was explicitly cancelled while only analyzer.mjs existed and before the required safeDump deliverable was finalized.
candidates.realized_consequence: The required dumper module was absent from the final artifact, leaving test16.mjs with an unresolved safeDump import and no complete YAML round-trip.
candidates.near_match_reason: The dumper assignment was broad, but the observable state transition that ended the work was explicit active-child cancellation before finalization.

candidates.reason: No complete, directly promotable full solution or compatible component set existed because the dumper was unfinished and cancelled.
The early verifier run is assigned to Incomplete Child Brief; there was no completed implementation merged after a valid integrated verification loop.
Completed child file writes landed directly in the shared output tree; the dumper implementation was not completed and therefore could not be joined.
The verifier child returned its completed report through the swarm result; the problem was that the report measured an incomplete state.
The child abort happened at run closure, and the same cancellation chain is captured by Early Child Termination rather than a distinct post-failure takeover decision.
The completed entry and verifier results were included in the final swarm output at closure; there is no separate parent decision that proceeded inconsistently after inspecting or ignoring them.
The parent waited on the swarm until timeout, but the directly evidenced adverse event is cancellation of the active dumper child, not an independent blind wait with available actionable progress.
Children wrote different expected files and no competing implementation designs for the same behavior required reconciliation.
No two live agents are shown editing the same source file and reconciling each other's concurrent changes.
There is no proven replacement or wholesale rewrite of another agent's non-entry source file.
The entry file was written by its assigned child and no later actor overwrote the deliverable.
No broad cleanup, rebuild, or promotion replaced multiple final outputs or invalidated another actor's final tree.
The shared workspace was used, but the observed adverse effects are better represented by the verifier brief and child cancellation, not an unisolated-write provenance problem.
The verifier did consume an incomplete tree, but that is the same episode retained as Incomplete Child Brief because the initial readiness instruction caused the consumption.

retained_patterns.reason: The verifier child was not given a sufficient readiness requirement for concurrent loader and dumper completion and therefore generated stale whole-task acceptance evidence.

retained_patterns.near_match_reason: The shared-tree contamination is downstream of the missing readiness requirement in the child brief.
